rv.q: Moment by moment, Bruni has it in great comedic shape, but no palpable human need drives the action and the stakes. Too fun to snooze, though.
An absolute riot — a truly original and genuinely laugh-out-loud story with tight pacing and structure.
Stiles not only gets the best number of the night — a knock-out song about menopause that will delight both the peri and the post — she gets off the best snark gags in the script.
It's funny — and occasionally very funny. But no matter how funny, 'Iceboy' suffers from its own iciness.
Two hours and 25 minutes of sheer beauty in comic storytelling — a comedy that would make Sondheim proud.
Flaws notwithstanding, I simply cannot imagine someone not enjoying themselves here.
If you want to see two very famous, very talented comic actors with Chicago roots doing exactly what they do best, then “Iceboy” is ideal.
Two acts of silly fun — but despite the whimsy, the production still feels like a work-in-progress, the next draft but perhaps not the final one.
Iceboy! could follow a similar trajectory—if it tightens up and loses about 20 percent of its overly campy, scatological slapstick.

Iceboy! has Megan Mullally, Nick Offerman, a defrosted caveman, and Eugene O’Neill — and somehow squanders all of it on a forgettable score and a script that never evolves past its own elevator pitch.
Capturing the feel of traditional musicals while incorporating new writing and comedy, Iceboy! enters into a new era of comedy shows.
But there’s not enough genuine emotional meat on the bones of this show for me.

cn.t: This absurd musical comedy about Eugene O'Neill earns laughs with its wacky premise and star power from Megan Mullally and Nick Offerman, though critics suggest it could benefit from tightening up its overly campy, stretched-out structure.
